title: A Beetle By Any Other Name

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In a valley in central Slovenia, there's a giant limestone cave called Pekel,
sentences.zh: 在斯洛文尼亚中部的一个山谷里，有一个巨大的石灰岩洞穴，名叫佩克尔（Pekel），

sentences.en: which means hell in Slovene.
sentences.zh: 在斯洛文尼亚语中，这个词的意思是“地狱”。

sentences.en: If you look hard at the rocks above the entrance,
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细观察入口上方的岩石，

sentences.en: you can just make out the shape of the devil,
sentences.zh: 你隐约能看出魔鬼的形状，

sentences.en: which is one explanation for how the cave got its name.
sentences.zh: 这也是该洞穴得名的一种解释。

sentences.en: That is British expat and 99PI's Slovenia correspondent, Will Aspinall.
sentences.zh: 那位是英国侨民，也是《99%隐形》驻斯洛文尼亚的通讯员，威尔·阿斯皮纳尔。

sentences.en: I recently met up with Andrzej Kapla from the Slovenian National Institute of Biology.
sentences.zh: 我最近见到了斯洛文尼亚国家生物研究所的安杰伊·卡普拉。

sentences.en: Andrzej studies the ecology of caves and today he is taking me spelunking.
sentences.zh: 安杰伊研究洞穴生态学，今天他要带我去探洞。

sentences.en: I'm not naturally inclined to go into caves.
sentences.zh: 我天生不太喜欢进洞穴。

sentences.en: Is it safe?
sentences.zh: 这安全吗？

sentences.en: It's completely safe.
sentences.zh: 非常安全。

sentences.en: But there's one caveat in this case because it was very, very rainy these days
sentences.zh: 但这次有个前提，因为这几天雨下得非常非常大，

sentences.en: and hopefully it didn't flood.
sentences.zh: 希望没有被淹。

sentences.en: But if it is flood, then we're in trouble.
sentences.zh: 如果被淹了，那我们就麻烦了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We're in the cave.
sentences.zh: 我们进洞了。

sentences.en: The cave is narrow, only about a metre wide in places,
sentences.zh: 洞穴很窄，有些地方只有一米宽，

sentences.en: but it's like 15 metres high.
sentences.zh: 但高度却有15米左右。

sentences.en: It's a chasm and it's flooded.
sentences.zh: 这是一个深渊，而且被水淹了。

sentences.en: Oh, it's beautiful.
sentences.zh: 噢，太美了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是啊，确实。

sentences.en: But wet.
sentences.zh: 就是有点湿。

sentences.en: You weren't scared of caves.
sentences.zh: 你以前不怕洞穴吗？

sentences.en: Never was.
sentences.zh: 从来不怕。

sentences.en: Actually, I'm more comfortable in a cave than with people.
sentences.zh: 其实，比起和人打交道，我待在洞穴里反而更自在。

sentences.en: Andrzej and I are not exploring a cave called Hell just for fun.
sentences.zh: 我和安杰伊探索这个叫“地狱”的洞穴可不是为了好玩。

sentences.en: We're on a mission to catch an elusive insect that Andrzej studies.
sentences.zh: 我们此行的任务是捕捉一种安杰伊正在研究的难以捉摸的昆虫。

sentences.en: A week earlier, he left seven traps inside the cave and baited them with a special recipe.
sentences.zh: 一周前，他在洞里留下了七个陷阱，并用一种特殊的配方作为诱饵。

sentences.en: It is a nice mixture of beef liver, fish and gorgonzola.
sentences.zh: 那是一种由牛肝、鱼肉和戈尔贡佐拉奶酪混合而成的美味。

sentences.en: You put them in a vals and marinate them for a few days on sun.
sentences.zh: 你把它们放进瓶子里，在阳光下腌制几天。

sentences.en: Absolutely disgusting.
sentences.zh: 简直恶心透了。

sentences.en: I'm trying to like these creatures.
sentences.zh: 我正试着去喜欢这些生物。

sentences.en: It's easy.
sentences.zh: 这很容易。

sentences.en: They're beautiful.
sentences.zh: 它们很美。

sentences.en: The beautiful creature that we are looking for has only been found in five caves in the north of Slovenia.
sentences.zh: 我们寻找的这种美丽生物目前只在斯洛文尼亚北部的五个洞穴中被发现过。

sentences.en: It's in a group of 51 known beetles called Anophthalmos, Greek for without eyes.
sentences.zh: 它属于51种已知甲虫中的一种，名为“Anophthalmos”，在希腊语中意为“无眼”。

sentences.en: These are not very big beetles.
sentences.zh: 这些甲虫并不大。

sentences.en: Nothing special about them.
sentences.zh: 没什么特别的。

sentences.en: More or less all look the same.
sentences.zh: 看起来都差不多。

sentences.en: So nothing special about other beetles.
sentences.zh: 所以其他甲虫也没什么特别的。

sentences.en: Just the name is special.
sentences.zh: 只有名字比较特别。

sentences.en: The beetle is notorious because it is named after arguably the worst human being in history.
sentences.zh: 这种甲虫之所以臭名昭著，是因为它以历史上最糟糕的人类命名。

sentences.en: We are hunting for Anophthalmos hitlery, more commonly known as Hitler's beetle.
sentences.zh: 我们正在寻找“Anophthalmos hitlery”，也就是俗称的“希特勒甲虫”。

sentences.en: Despite living in complete darkness in a handful of caves in a tiny Central European country,
sentences.zh: 尽管它生活在欧洲中部一个小国少数几个洞穴的完全黑暗中，

sentences.en: this unremarkable insect is getting a lot of unwelcome attention right now.
sentences.zh: 这种不起眼的昆虫现在却受到了许多不必要的关注。

sentences.en: Hitler's beetle is at the center of a fierce debate raging in the usually polite worlds of botany and zoology.
sentences.zh: 希特勒甲虫正处于植物学和动物学这两个通常很文雅的领域中一场激烈辩论的中心。

sentences.en: It's a debate about whether we should rename species that are named after objectionable human beings,
sentences.zh: 这场辩论的主题是：我们是否应该为以令人反感的人物命名的物种改名，

sentences.en: and even whether we should be naming organisms after people at all.
sentences.zh: 甚至我们是否应该以人的名字来命名生物。

sentences.en: Plants and animals have no say over what we humans call them.
sentences.zh: 动植物无法决定人类如何称呼它们。

sentences.en: But it turns out a controversial scientific name can profoundly impact how a species fares in the real world.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，一个有争议的学名会深刻影响一个物种在现实世界中的生存状况。

sentences.en: The practice of naming species after humans goes back to the 18th century in a man named Carl Linnaeus.
sentences.zh: 以人名命名物种的做法可以追溯到18世纪，始于一位名叫卡尔·林奈的人。

sentences.en: Linnaeus was a really interesting character.
sentences.zh: 林奈是一个非常有趣的人物。

sentences.en: So he was a Swedish botaniSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位瑞典植物学家。

sentences.en: Sandy Knapp is also a botanist and the author of In the Name of Plants,
sentences.zh: 桑迪·纳普也是一位植物学家，著有《以植物之名》一书，

sentences.en: Remarkable Plants and the Extraordinary People Behind Their Names.
sentences.zh: 全名是《非凡的植物与它们名字背后的非凡人物》。

sentences.en: He was a Swedish doctor, actually, because in the 18th century, which is when Linnaeus lived,
sentences.zh: 其实他还是位瑞典医生，因为在林奈生活的18世纪，

sentences.en: medicine was entirely based on plants.
sentences.zh: 医学完全基于植物。

sentences.en: He was also incredibly arrogant and he was convinced that he could just completely reform how we understood nature.
sentences.zh: 他也非常傲慢，坚信自己可以彻底改革我们对自然的理解。

sentences.en: Today, his arrogance seems justified because he more or less met that lofty goal.
sentences.zh: 今天，他的傲慢似乎是合理的，因为他或多或少实现了那个宏伟的目标。

sentences.en: Linnaeus found order in the chaos of the natural world by creating a new framework for naming and categorizing every known animal and plant.
sentences.zh: 林奈通过建立一套新的框架来命名和分类每一种已知的动植物，在混乱的自然界中找到了秩序。

sentences.en: Before Linnaeus, the names of organisms were really more like sentences.
sentences.zh: 在林奈之前，生物的名字更像是句子。

sentences.en: So it would be a thing like, this is the plant that has white flowers with yellow bits in the middle and leaves which are slightly incised at the edges.
sentences.zh: 比如，这是一种花朵呈白色、中间有黄色斑点、叶子边缘略有缺口的植物。

sentences.en: So that would be the name of the plant.
sentences.zh: 那就会是这种植物的名字。

sentences.en: Linnaeus knew this was really cumbersome.
sentences.zh: 林奈知道这非常繁琐。

sentences.en: And so he came up with a simpler naming convention.
sentences.zh: 于是他想出了一种更简单的命名惯例。

sentences.en: He gave every plant and animal a two-word name in either Latin or ancient Greek.
sentences.zh: 他给每种动植物起了一个拉丁语或古希腊语的双词名称。

sentences.en: To take a well-known example, Linnaeus called human beings Homo sapiens.
sentences.zh: 举个众所周知的例子，林奈称人类为“智人”（Homo sapiens）。

sentences.en: The first word, homo, meaning man, is a broad category, the genus.
sentences.zh: 第一个词“Homo”，意为“人”，是一个广泛的类别，即属名。

sentences.en: And then sapiens, which means wise or thinking, is the specific name or the species.
sentences.zh: 而“sapiens”，意为“智慧的”或“思考的”，是具体名称，即种加词。

sentences.en: Together, the genus and species are combined to create a scientific name that's both unique and easy to remember.
sentences.zh: 属名和种加词结合在一起，构成了一个既独特又易于记忆的学名。

sentences.en: This became Linnaeus' binomial system.
sentences.zh: 这就是林奈的二名法系统。

sentences.en: And over time, this concise piece of information design was picked up by scientists all across Europe.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，这种简洁的信息设计被全欧洲的科学家所采用。

sentences.en: And I think it took off because essentially it replicates the noun adjective construction of things that we have in most languages.
sentences.zh: 我认为它之所以流行，是因为它本质上复制了我们在大多数语言中使用的“名词+形容词”结构。

sentences.en: We have bicycles, which is the genus, and we have red bicycles and green bicycles and golden bicycles and little bicycles.
sentences.zh: 我们有自行车，这是属，然后我们有红色的自行车、绿色的自行车、金色的自行车和小型的自行车。

sentences.en: But it wasn't inevitable that Linnaeus' binomial system would become the standard.
sentences.zh: 但林奈的二名法系统并非必然会成为标准。

sentences.en: At the time, there were lots of weird and, frankly, confusing alternatives.
sentences.zh: 当时，有很多奇怪且坦率地说令人困惑的替代方案。

sentences.en: My favourite is one that was published in, oh, I don't know, about 1760 by someone called Bergeret in France.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的是1760年左右由法国一位名叫贝尔热雷的人发表的一种系统。

sentences.en: In Bergeret's system, each letter of a plant's name corresponded to some aspect of its biology.
sentences.zh: 在贝尔热雷的系统中，植物名称的每个字母都对应其生物学的一个方面。

sentences.en: The idea was that the name could communicate important information about the species, but it looked like a jumble of seemingly random letters.
sentences.zh: 其理念是名称可以传达有关物种的重要信息，但看起来就像一堆看似随机的字母组合。

sentences.en: The name of the plant was the combination of those letters, so it was B-R-Q-X-W.
sentences.zh: 植物的名字就是这些字母的组合，比如B-R-Q-X-W。

sentences.en: You know, I just love it when the B-R-Q-X-Ws are flowering in the spring.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我就是喜欢春天里B-R-Q-X-W开花的样子。

sentences.en: Is that easier to remember than Atropa belladonna for the deadly nightshade?
sentences.zh: 这比用“Atropa belladonna”来称呼颠茄更容易记住吗？

sentences.en: And you can see why Linnaeus' system caught on.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出为什么林奈的系统会流行起来。

sentences.en: Linnaeus was also a brilliant teacher.
sentences.zh: 林奈也是一位出色的老师。

sentences.en: And at Uppsala University, just north of Stockholm, he inspired the brightest and bravest young men to go out and explore the natural world.
sentences.zh: 在斯德哥尔摩北部的乌普萨拉大学，他激励了最聪明、最勇敢的年轻人去探索自然世界。

sentences.en: They were called his apostles, but these were his students who basically went out.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为他的“使徒”，这些学生基本上都走出了国门。

sentences.en: He sent them out around the world to collect plants in different parts of the world because at that time that was beginning to become possible.
sentences.zh: 他派他们到世界各地去采集植物，因为在那个时代，这开始变得可行了。

sentences.en: His apostles travelled the world on dangerous scientific missions.
sentences.zh: 他的使徒们踏上了危险的科学考察之旅，走遍全球。

sentences.en: To Java and Japan, Venezuela and Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 去往爪哇和日本、委内瑞拉和越南。

sentences.en: Many of them lost their lives to tropical diseases, and Linnaeus decided to honour their contributions to science by naming organisms after them.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人死于热带疾病，林奈决定通过以他们的名字命名生物来纪念他们对科学的贡献。

sentences.en: To use Sally's analogy, not only were there red bicycles and yellow bicycles, but there were now Will's bicycles and Roman's bicycles too.
sentences.zh: 用萨利的类比来说，现在不仅有红色的自行车和黄色的自行车，还有威尔的自行车和罗曼的自行车。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just his apostles.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是他的使徒。

sentences.en: Linnaeus also named plants after scientists he admired.
sentences.zh: 林奈还以他钦佩的科学家的名字命名植物。

sentences.en: Take, for example, the magnolia.
sentences.zh: 以木兰花（Magnolia）为例。

sentences.en: Pierre Magnol was a botanist who wrote a flora of the area around Montpellier and was one of the people who sort of first came up with the concept of plants having families,
sentences.zh: 皮埃尔·马格诺尔是一位植物学家，他编写了蒙彼利埃地区的植物志，是首批提出植物有“科”这一概念的人之一，

sentences.en: plants being in families.
sentences.zh: 即植物属于不同的科。

sentences.en: Linnaeus was a great admirer of magnols, so he named magnolia for magnol.
sentences.zh: 林奈非常钦佩马格诺尔，所以他用马格诺尔的名字命名了木兰属。

sentences.en: But Linnaeus was clear that not just anyone should be given the honour of having a species or a genus named after them.
sentences.zh: 但林奈明确表示，并不是随便什么人都能获得以其名字命名物种或属的荣誉。

sentences.en: He even wrote down guidelines about what type of person was acceptable.
sentences.zh: 他甚至写下了关于什么样的人可以被接受的指导方针。

sentences.en: They weren't rules as in you had to follow them, but they were his rules for how things should be done properly.
sentences.zh: 这些不是必须遵守的规则，而是他关于如何正确行事的准则。

sentences.en: Things like names should not be used to gain the favour or preserve the memory of saints or of men famous in some other art.
sentences.zh: 比如，名字不应被用来博取圣人的青睐，或纪念在其他艺术领域成名的人。

sentences.en: So his view was that you should name things for people who have promoted the science of botany.
sentences.zh: 所以他的观点是，你应该以那些推动了植物学科学发展的人的名字来命名事物。

sentences.en: Linnaeus named 12,000 species in his lifetime, and actually very few of those were named after people.
sentences.zh: 林奈一生命名了12000个物种，实际上以人名命名的寥寥无几。

sentences.en: But in the centuries that followed, as more and more plants and animals got discovered, the practice became increasingly common.
sentences.zh: 但在随后的几个世纪里，随着越来越多的动植物被发现，这种做法变得越来越普遍。

sentences.en: And Linnaeus' guidelines about what kind of people you should name a species after went more or less out the window.
sentences.zh: 而林奈关于应该以什么样的人命名物种的指导方针也基本被抛诸脑后了。

sentences.en: Increasingly, scientists began to name species after people they just happened to be fond of.
sentences.zh: 科学家们开始越来越多地以他们恰好喜欢的人的名字来命名物种。

sentences.en: Slovenia's infamous beetle was very nearly given a different name.
sentences.zh: 斯洛文尼亚那只臭名昭著的甲虫差点被赋予了另一个名字。

sentences.en: The insect was discovered in 1932 by a Slovenian naturalist named Vladimir Kodrich in a cave very close to the one I visited with Andrzej.
sentences.zh: 这种昆虫是1932年由一位名叫弗拉基米尔·科德里奇的斯洛文尼亚博物学家在离我与安杰伊访问的洞穴很近的地方发现的。

sentences.en: Kodrich thought he had found a new species, but he wanted a second opinion.
sentences.zh: 科德里奇认为他发现了一个新物种，但他想听听第二意见。

sentences.en: And so he sent a specimen to an Austrian beetle collector called Oskar Scheibel.
sentences.zh: 于是他把标本寄给了一位名叫奥斯卡·沙伊贝尔的奥地利甲虫收藏家。

sentences.en: Oskar Scheibel was actually a very good entomologiSt.
sentences.zh: 奥斯卡·沙伊贝尔实际上是一位非常优秀的昆虫学家。

sentences.en: He had money, so he could afford to go to trips.
sentences.zh: 他有钱，所以负担得起旅行费用。

sentences.en: He could afford to buy specimens from people like Mr. Kodrich.
sentences.zh: 他负担得起从像科德里奇先生这样的人那里购买标本。

sentences.en: And he had vast knowledge about this.
sentences.zh: 而且他对此有渊博的知识。

sentences.en: Scheibel confirmed that the beetle was a new species.
sentences.zh: 沙伊贝尔证实该甲虫确实是一个新物种。

sentences.en: And, adhering to Linnaeus' guidelines, he initially agreed to name the new beetle Anophthalmus Kodrichi to honor the discoverer.
sentences.zh: 并且，遵循林奈的指导方针，他最初同意将这种新甲虫命名为“Anophthalmus kodrichi”，以纪念发现者。

sentences.en: But then he had a radical change of heart.
sentences.zh: 但随后他的想法发生了根本性的转变。

sentences.en: Because in addition to being a world-famous bug collector...
sentences.zh: 因为除了作为世界著名的昆虫收藏家之外……

sentences.en: Unfortunately, he was a passionate Nazi.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他还是一个狂热的纳粹分子。

sentences.en: And so, Scheibel's formal submission of Anophthalmus Hitlerei in a German scientific journal in 1937 combined his two great loves, entomology and Adolf Hitler.
sentences.zh: 因此，沙伊贝尔于1937年在一家德国科学期刊上正式提交了“Anophthalmus hitlerei”，结合了他两大挚爱：昆虫学和阿道夫·希特勒。

sentences.en: Hitler was apparently quite tickled by this gesture.
sentences.zh: 希特勒显然对这一举动感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: According to some sources, he sent a personal letter to Scheibel thanking him for the honor.
sentences.zh: 据一些消息来源称，他给沙伊贝尔写了一封亲笔信，感谢他的这一荣誉。

sentences.en: Naming a species after Hitler might be particularly ill-advised, but this kind of thing happens all the time.
sentences.zh: 以希特勒的名字命名物种可能特别不明智，但这种事情时有发生。

sentences.en: There are around 2 million known species in the world today.
sentences.zh: 当今世界上大约有200万种已知物种。

sentences.en: Each year, another 18,000 get discovered.
sentences.zh: 每年又有18000种被发现。

sentences.en: And every new species needs a name.
sentences.zh: 每一个新物种都需要一个名字。

sentences.en: Which has led to some, shall we say, interesting choices.
sentences.zh: 这导致了一些，我们姑且称之为“有趣”的选择。

sentences.en: We did so much field work and went to so many different sites that, you know, those first few months when we first started, we're like, oh man, look at this new species.
sentences.zh: 我们做了大量的实地考察，去了很多不同的地点，你知道，刚开始的那几个月，我们就像是，天哪，看看这个新物种。

sentences.en: We were really excited.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很兴奋。

sentences.en: But we just kept finding more and more and more.
sentences.zh: 但我们只是不断地发现更多、更多、更多。

sentences.en: This is Derek Hennon.
sentences.zh: 这位是德里克·亨农。

sentences.en: He's a diplodologiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位倍足纲动物学家。

sentences.en: That's a person who studies millipedes.
sentences.zh: 也就是研究马陆的人。

sentences.en: In 2021 and 2022, Derek and two colleagues from Virginia Tech published several papers based on years researching the millipedes of Appalachia.
sentences.zh: 2021年和2022年，德里克和弗吉尼亚理工大学的两位同事发表了几篇基于多年研究阿巴拉契亚马陆的论文。

sentences.en: Over that time, they discovered 50 new millipede species, and each one needed a name.
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里，他们发现了50种新的马陆物种，每一种都需要一个名字。

sentences.en: When you have 50 new species to name, you're really trying to pull from anything to kind of make them unique and also just to sound different.
sentences.zh: 当你需要为50个新物种命名时，你真的会试图从任何地方寻找灵感，让它们既独特又听起来与众不同。

sentences.en: They named some millipedes for the location where they were found, like Ninaria scholastica, discovered on the campus of Washington and Lee University in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 他们以发现地点命名了一些马陆，比如在弗吉尼亚州华盛顿与李大学校园发现的“Ninaria scholastica”。

sentences.en: Others got names related to how they looked, like Ninaria serpents, a millipede with distinctly snake-like features.
sentences.zh: 其他的名字则与它们的外观有关，比如“Ninaria serpents”，这是一种具有明显蛇类特征的马陆。

sentences.en: But with so many new millipedes, place names and simple adjectives wouldn't suffice.
sentences.zh: 但随着这么多新马陆的出现，地名和简单的形容词已经不够用了。

sentences.en: And so they decided to name some of them after people.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定以人的名字来命名其中的一些。

sentences.en: And if you want an obscure millipede to stand out, why not name it after one of the most famous and beloved people on the planet?
sentences.zh: 如果你想让一种默默无闻的马陆脱颖而出，为什么不用地球上最著名、最受欢迎的人之一的名字来命名它呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, first, I would say, you know, I was just a fan of Taylor Swift's music.
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，首先，我会说，你知道，我只是泰勒·斯威夫特音乐的粉丝。

sentences.en: And we'd be driving to these field sites, and, you know, I would like to play Taylor Swift when I could.
sentences.zh: 我们开车去这些实地考察点时，你知道，我喜欢在可能的时候播放泰勒·斯威夫特的歌。

sentences.en: And so, you know, kind of as a nod to her music keeping me in a good mood when I needed it, I wanted to name a species after her.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，为了感谢她的音乐在我需要的时候让我保持好心情，我想以她的名字命名一个物种。

sentences.en: When Derek named a millipede Ninaria Swifty after the world's biggest pop star, he became perhaps the first diplodologist to be featured in the pages of Rolling Stone.
sentences.zh: 当德里克以这位世界顶级流行巨星的名字命名马陆“Ninaria swifty”时，他可能成为了第一位登上《滚石》杂志的倍足纲动物学家。

sentences.en: Which was great because, you know, normally millipedes don't make front-page news too often, so it was a fun experience.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了，因为你知道，通常马陆不会经常上头条新闻，所以这是一次有趣的经历。

sentences.en: And, you know, I was just glad to have people excited about millipedes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我很高兴人们对马陆感到兴奋。

sentences.en: Taylor Swift wasn't the only human being Derek honoured.
sentences.zh: 泰勒·斯威夫特并不是德里克纪念的唯一人类。

sentences.en: Famous podcasters, the McElroy brothers, also have a millipede named after them.
sentences.zh: 著名的播客组合麦克尔罗伊兄弟，也有一种马陆以他们的名字命名。

sentences.en: And crawling around at the bottom of Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains is Ninaria Mariani, named after Derek's wife.
sentences.zh: 而在弗吉尼亚州蓝岭山脉底部爬行的，是尼纳里亚·马里亚尼（Ninaria Mariani），它以德瑞克的妻子命名。

sentences.en: My wife often goes out with me when I want to look for millipedes,
sentences.zh: 当我想要寻找马陆时，我妻子经常会陪我一起去，

sentences.en: and so that was also just to show her my appreciation for how patient she is to wait for me as I am digging around in the leaves.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是为了向她表达我的感激，感谢她在我翻找落叶时耐心地等待我。

sentences.en: These days, lots of scientists are pulling stunts like this.
sentences.zh: 如今，许多科学家都在玩这种把戏。

sentences.en: There's a horsefly named Scaptia Beyoncé, and a tiny Mexican moth named Wakia Chewbacca.
sentences.zh: 有一种马蝇叫碧昂丝马蝇（Scaptia beyonceae），还有一种微小的墨西哥蛾子叫楚巴卡蛾（Wakia chewbacca）。

sentences.en: Arnold Schwarzenegger has two insects named after him, a beetle called Agra Schwarzeneggeri,
sentences.zh: 阿诺德·施瓦辛格就有两种昆虫以他的名字命名，一种是名为“施瓦辛格步甲”（Agra schwarzeneggeri）的甲虫，

sentences.en: and a tiny fly with oversized legs called Megapropodifora Arnoldi.
sentences.zh: 还有一种腿部超大的微型苍蝇，名为“阿诺德巨足蝇”（Megapropodifora arnoldi）。

sentences.en: And not all the names are cute and fun.
sentences.zh: 而且并非所有的命名都既可爱又有趣。

sentences.en: Some scientists clearly have a political agenda.
sentences.zh: 有些科学家显然有政治意图。

sentences.en: In 2005, entomologists Kelly Miller and Quentin Wheeler named a trio of slime mold beetles after Bush, Cheney, and Rumsfeld.
sentences.zh: 2005年，昆虫学家凯利·米勒和昆汀·惠勒以布什、切尼和拉姆斯菲尔德的名字命名了三种粘菌甲虫。

sentences.en: Announced at the height of the Iraq war, it seemed like a subversive act.
sentences.zh: 在伊拉克战争最激烈的时候宣布这一消息，看起来像是一种颠覆性的行为。

sentences.en: People thought they're slime mold beetles.
sentences.zh: 人们以为它们是粘菌甲虫。

sentences.en: He must be kind of making a joke about how awful these people are.
sentences.zh: 他一定是在开玩笑，讽刺这些人有多糟糕。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: Quentin was a great admirer of the Republican administration at the time,
sentences.zh: 昆汀当时非常钦佩那届共和党政府，

sentences.en: and so he named those beetles to honor those men.
sentences.zh: 所以他命名这些甲虫是为了向这些人致敬。

sentences.en: My first instinct was that these names were mostly harmless.
sentences.zh: 我的第一直觉是，这些名字大多是无害的。

sentences.en: If hard-working zoologists want to shine a light on their relatively arcane work
sentences.zh: 如果勤奋的动物学家想要通过用他们最喜欢的播客主或政治家的名字来命名萤火虫，

sentences.en: by naming a glowworm after their favorite podcaster or politician, who am I to judge?
sentences.zh: 从而让人们关注他们相对冷门的研究，我有什么资格评判呢？

sentences.en: But sometimes a name is so loaded that it can cause very real problems for the unfortunate creature.
sentences.zh: 但有时一个名字所承载的含义太重，可能会给这种不幸的生物带来非常现实的问题。

sentences.en: Which brings us back to Hitler's beetle.
sentences.zh: 这就让我们回到了希特勒甲虫的话题。

sentences.en: 20 years ago, Andrei Kapler made a grim discovery in the cave where Anophthalmus Hitleri was first found.
sentences.zh: 20年前，安德烈·卡普勒在最初发现希特勒盲步甲（Anophthalmus hitleri）的洞穴中有一个严峻的发现。

sentences.en: Poachers had destroyed the fragile cave ecosystem, and the ground was littered with beetle traps.
sentences.zh: 偷猎者破坏了脆弱的洞穴生态系统，地面上到处都是甲虫陷阱。

sentences.en: It turns out Hitler's beetle is in high demand from far-right extremists who are buying up dead specimens like tiny Nazi trophies.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，希特勒甲虫在极右翼极端分子中需求量很大，他们像收集纳粹战利品一样购买这些死标本。

sentences.en: Every specimen is precious because we need it for research, not for showcasing them and boasting around.
sentences.zh: 每一个标本都很珍贵，因为我们需要它进行研究，而不是拿来炫耀和吹嘘。

sentences.en: Oh, look what I have.
sentences.zh: 噢，看看我有什么。

sentences.en: I have Hitler's beetle.
sentences.zh: 我有希特勒甲虫。

sentences.en: That's stupid.
sentences.zh: 那太蠢了。

sentences.en: Preserved insects have been pillaged from museums in Germany.
sentences.zh: 德国博物馆里的昆虫标本曾遭到洗劫。

sentences.en: And in December 2023, the New York Times reported that specimens of Hitler's beetle were going for as much as $2,000.
sentences.zh: 2023年12月，《纽约时报》报道称，希特勒甲虫的标本售价高达2000美元。

sentences.en: Andrei believes that's a huge exaggeration, and the real price is a fraction of that.
sentences.zh: 安德烈认为这太夸张了，实际价格只有那的一小部分。

sentences.en: But the poaching is definitely real.
sentences.zh: 但偷猎行为绝对是真实存在的。

sentences.en: In 2004, the Slovenian government introduced a law to protect underground creatures like Anophthalmus Hitleri,
sentences.zh: 2004年，斯洛文尼亚政府出台了一项法律，旨在保护像希特勒盲步甲这样的地下生物，

sentences.en: and the original cave was closed to the public.
sentences.zh: 最初的那个洞穴也对公众关闭了。

sentences.en: And while it's unlikely that Hitler's beetle will get poached to extinction by neo-Nazis,
sentences.zh: 虽然希特勒甲虫不太可能因为新纳粹分子的偷猎而灭绝，

sentences.en: it's clear that the insect's terrible name is not making it any safer.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，这种昆虫糟糕的名字并没有让它变得更安全。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, the moment of truth.
sentences.zh: 现在，见证时刻到了。

sentences.en: Andrei and I are back in the cave called Hell, and we're checking his beetle traps.
sentences.zh: 我和安德烈回到了那个叫“地狱”的洞穴，我们正在检查他的甲虫陷阱。

sentences.en: OK, it's the first trap.
sentences.zh: 好的，这是第一个陷阱。

sentences.en: It is the firSt.
sentences.zh: 这是第一个。

sentences.en: Nothing?
sentences.zh: 什么都没有？

sentences.en: But sadly, we are striking out.
sentences.zh: 但遗憾的是，我们一无所获。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: God damn it.
sentences.zh: 该死。

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有。

sentences.en: Andrei says our struggles on today's beetle hunt have very little to do with neo-Nazis,
sentences.zh: 安德烈说，我们今天甲虫狩猎的困境与新纳粹分子几乎没有关系，

sentences.en: and everything to do with the heavy rainfall we've been getting.
sentences.zh: 而与我们最近经历的强降雨有很大关系。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不。

sentences.en: This one got slanted.
sentences.zh: 这个倾斜了。

sentences.en: OK, is that number five?
sentences.zh: 好的，那是五号吗？

sentences.en: Number five has got water in it.
sentences.zh: 五号里面进水了。

sentences.en: But the others were dry, just didn't have any of Hitler's beetle.
sentences.zh: 但其他的都是干的，只是没有希特勒甲虫。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This is the last one.
sentences.zh: 这是最后一个。

sentences.en: The last one.
sentences.zh: 最后一个。

sentences.en: And it's empty.
sentences.zh: 它是空的。

sentences.en: Does that surprise you?
sentences.zh: 这让你感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: You have to be extremely patient with the cave beetles.
sentences.zh: 对于洞穴甲虫，你必须非常有耐心。

sentences.en: So it may take, sometimes it takes years and years just to catch one.
sentences.zh: 所以可能需要，有时需要好几年才能抓到一只。

sentences.en: So, it's not a tragedy, it's just misfortune.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不算悲剧，只是运气不好。

sentences.en: Coming up after the break, should Hitler's beetle get a new name?
sentences.zh: 休息之后，希特勒甲虫应该改名吗？

sentences.en: Everyone who I interviewed for this story more or less agreed
sentences.zh: 我为这个故事采访过的每个人都或多或少地同意，

sentences.en: that the name Hitler's beetle was an unfortunate historical relic,
sentences.zh: 希特勒甲虫这个名字是一个不幸的历史遗迹，

sentences.en: which begs the question, why not just change it?
sentences.zh: 这就引出了一个问题，为什么不直接改掉它呢？

sentences.en: After all, it wouldn't be the first time.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这也不是第一次了。

sentences.en: Shortly after World War II, Hitler's name was erased from roads and town squares all across Europe and beyond.
sentences.zh: 二战结束后不久，希特勒的名字就从欧洲及其他地区的道路和城镇广场上被抹去了。

sentences.en: Residents of Park Boulevard and Jaapank, Long Island,
sentences.zh: 长岛公园大道和贾潘克（Jaapank）的居民，

sentences.en: might be blissfully unaware that Nazi sympathizers once named it Adolf Hitler Street.
sentences.zh: 可能根本不知道纳粹同情者曾经把它命名为阿道夫·希特勒街。

sentences.en: So if we can take Hitler's name off street signs, why can't we remove him from the natural world?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们能把希特勒的名字从路牌上拿掉，为什么不能把他从自然界中移除呢？

sentences.en: It turns out that the international bodies that govern these matters are not big fans of change.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，管理这些事务的国际机构并不太喜欢改变。

sentences.en: The International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature, or ICZN, are responsible for the naming of animals.
sentences.zh: 国际动物命名法委员会（ICZN）负责动物的命名。

sentences.en: And they say that they have no power to change a name based on how offensive it is,
sentences.zh: 他们表示，他们无权根据名字的冒犯程度来更改名字，

sentences.en: a stance that's been getting a lot of heat in recent years.
sentences.zh: 这一立场近年来受到了很多抨击。

sentences.en: It's a remarkably controversial subject, far more controversial than I ever imagined.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常具有争议的话题，比我预想的要争议得多。

sentences.en: I've been publishing scientific articles for 30 years now,
sentences.zh: 我发表科学文章已经30年了，

sentences.en: and this has got the most amount of interest of anything that I've ever published.
sentences.zh: 这是我发表过的所有文章中引起关注最多的一篇。

sentences.en: Richard Ladle is Professor of Conservation Science at the Federal University of Alagoas in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 理查德·拉德尔是巴西阿拉戈斯联邦大学的保护科学教授。

sentences.en: He was one of 11 scientists who co-authored an article in the journal Nature, Ecology and Evolution,
sentences.zh: 他是《自然-生态与演化》杂志上一篇论文的11位合著者之一，

sentences.en: arguing not only that offensive names like Anophthalmos hitlery should be changed,
sentences.zh: 他们不仅主张应该更改像希特勒盲步甲这样具有冒犯性的名字，

sentences.en: but we should also stop the practice of naming animals after humans entirely.
sentences.zh: 还主张我们应该完全停止以人类名字命名动物的做法。

sentences.en: Do you want a species to be a living reminder?
sentences.zh: 你希望一个物种成为活生生的提醒吗？

sentences.en: Because that's what it is.
sentences.zh: 因为事实就是这样。

sentences.en: You know, it's a living reminder of something that maybe doesn't deserve to be celebrated.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它是一个活生生的提醒，提醒人们某种可能不值得被歌颂的事物。

sentences.en: Richard's main contribution to the paper was to provide some startling data.
sentences.zh: 理查德对这篇论文的主要贡献是提供了一些惊人的数据。

sentences.en: In Africa alone, a quarter of all vertebrates are named after people,
sentences.zh: 仅在非洲，四分之一的脊椎动物是以人名命名的，

sentences.en: and a large portion of these people are white British men and women from the 19th and early 20th centuries.
sentences.zh: 而这些人中很大一部分是19世纪和20世纪初的白人英国男女。

sentences.en: Europe's grim legacy still grows, walks, flies and swims in the habitats of these once colonised lands.
sentences.zh: 欧洲那段严峻的遗产，依然在这些曾经被殖民的土地上生长、行走、飞翔和游动。

sentences.en: I remember going to London Zoo and seeing Lady Amherst's pheasant, which is just the most amazing looking bird.
sentences.zh: 我记得去伦敦动物园看到白腹锦鸡，那真是一种看起来最令人惊叹的鸟。

sentences.en: And it's from China.
sentences.zh: 它来自中国。

sentences.en: You know, it could be the symbol of China.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它本可以成为中国的象征。

sentences.en: It's that amazing.
sentences.zh: 它就是那么令人惊叹。

sentences.en: It's one of the most beautiful birds in the world, named after a posh English woman.
sentences.zh: 它是世界上最美丽的鸟类之一，却以一位时髦的英国女性的名字命名。

sentences.en: To Richard, the morality of this is pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 对理查德来说，这背后的道德问题很清楚。

sentences.en: But before the paper had even gone out, he was already getting the sense that not everyone in the scientific community agreed with him.
sentences.zh: 但在论文发表之前，他就已经感觉到科学界并非所有人都同意他的观点。

sentences.en: One of the heads of his institution even urged him not to publish.
sentences.zh: 他所在机构的一位负责人甚至敦促他不要发表。

sentences.en: At which time I started to panic, because then I realised, I realised that the s*** was really going to hit the fan.
sentences.zh: 当时我开始恐慌，因为我意识到，我意识到事情真的要闹大了。

sentences.en: When the article finally came out in March 2023, many of his peers were outraged.
sentences.zh: 当这篇文章最终在2023年3月发表时，他的许多同行感到愤怒。

sentences.en: I was totally stunned how passionate some taxonomists were against this idea.
sentences.zh: 我完全震惊于一些分类学家对这个想法的反对是多么激烈。

sentences.en: The main argument against Richard's proposal is maintaining scientific continuity.
sentences.zh: 反对理查德提议的主要论点是保持科学的连续性。

sentences.en: Right now, the ICZN will only change names if further research causes the status of an animal to be revised,
sentences.zh: 目前，ICZN只有在进一步研究导致动物地位发生修订时才会更改名称，

sentences.en: from, say, a subspecies to a full species.
sentences.zh: 比如，从亚种修订为完整物种。

sentences.en: They're conservative about change because they don't want to disrupt the chain of scientific knowledge
sentences.zh: 他们对改变持保守态度，因为他们不想破坏科学知识的链条，

sentences.en: that goes all the way back to Linnaeus.
sentences.zh: 那个链条一直追溯到林奈。

sentences.en: For Richard, that feels like an excuse for inaction.
sentences.zh: 对理查德来说，这听起来像是无所作为的借口。

sentences.en: He says that too often, scientists regard themselves as being above politics.
sentences.zh: 他说，科学家们太经常认为自己凌驾于政治之上。

sentences.en: The fundamental aspect of this, that naming something is a political act,
sentences.zh: 这件事情的根本在于，命名本身就是一种政治行为，

sentences.en: and, you know, pretending that it isn't, is not particularly intellectually honeSt.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，假装它不是，在智识上并不诚实。

sentences.en: And for any political act, we need to think about the potential consequences,
sentences.zh: 对于任何政治行为，我们都需要考虑潜在的后果，

sentences.en: not just now, but in the future.
sentences.zh: 不仅是现在，还有未来。

sentences.en: At the very least, Richard thinks scientists should challenge themselves
sentences.zh: 至少，理查德认为科学家应该挑战自己，

sentences.en: to get more creative and specific when naming new species.
sentences.zh: 在命名新物种时变得更有创意和针对性。

sentences.en: If you have to name 200 new species, that's difficult.
sentences.zh: 如果你必须命名200个新物种，那很难。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's not that difficult.
sentences.zh: 是的，但也没那么难。

sentences.en: Get a map out.
sentences.zh: 拿出一张地图。

sentences.en: There are ways to do this.
sentences.zh: 有很多方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Crowdsource it.
sentences.zh: 众包。

sentences.en: Use local words.
sentences.zh: 使用当地语言。

sentences.en: Use local landmarks.
sentences.zh: 使用当地地标。

sentences.en: There's countless possibilities.
sentences.zh: 有无数种可能性。

sentences.en: Richard is not short of ideas, and throughout our lively Zoom call,
sentences.zh: 理查德不缺创意，在我们整个生动的Zoom通话中，

sentences.en: I have to say, he made a convincing advocate for change.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，他是一个令人信服的变革倡导者。

sentences.en: Yeah, I really feel we ought to give a bit more respect to nature,
sentences.zh: 是的，我真的觉得我们应该对自然多一点尊重，

sentences.en: and especially when we're naming it.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在我们为它命名的时候。

sentences.en: But botanist Sandy Knapp is not totally convinced by Richard Ladle's proposal.
sentences.zh: 但植物学家桑迪·纳普并不完全被理查德·拉德尔的提议所说服。

sentences.en: She believes that changing all the species that are named after people
sentences.zh: 她认为，更改所有以人名命名的物种，

sentences.en: would be a monumental undertaking.
sentences.zh: 将是一项巨大的工程。

sentences.en: There are thousands of names of things that are named for people.
sentences.zh: 有成千上万的事物是以人名命名的。

sentences.en: Thousands and thousands.
sentences.zh: 成千上万。

sentences.en: And it's not like there's one master spreadsheet
sentences.zh: 而且并不是有一个总电子表格，

sentences.en: that you can just edit one time and be done with.
sentences.zh: 你可以一次性编辑完就大功告成。

sentences.en: Sandy says that going through and trying to change all those names
sentences.zh: 桑迪说，去逐一尝试更改所有这些名字，

sentences.en: in the countless places they appear would be extremely time-consuming
sentences.zh: 在它们出现的无数地方进行修改，将极其耗时，

sentences.en: and an unnecessary distraction from much more pressing concerns.
sentences.zh: 而且会分散人们对更紧迫问题的注意力，是不必要的。

sentences.en: Time is a resource.
sentences.zh: 时间是一种资源。

sentences.en: And there's way more important things to do than changing all the names.
sentences.zh: 比起更改所有的名字，还有更重要的事情要做。

sentences.en: I mean, we're in the middle of a planetary emergency
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们正处于全球紧急状态，

sentences.en: and a biodiversity crisis.
sentences.zh: 以及生物多样性危机之中。

sentences.en: And so do we want to find out more about biodiversity
sentences.zh: 所以，我们是想了解更多关于生物多样性的信息，

sentences.en: and how to preserve it and restore it?
sentences.zh: 以及如何保护和恢复它？

sentences.en: Or do we want to spend our time changing the names of things?
sentences.zh: 还是想把时间花在更改事物的名字上？

sentences.en: To me, that's the choice.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就是选择。

sentences.en: Currently, the ICZN have no appetite for taxonomical revolution.
sentences.zh: 目前，ICZN对分类学革命毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: But the ICN, or the International Code of Nomenclature for Algae, Fungi, and Plants,
sentences.zh: 但ICN，即《国际藻类、真菌和植物命名法规》，

sentences.en: has recently removed some offensive names.
sentences.zh: 最近已经删除了一些冒犯性的名字。

sentences.en: And although she isn't a fan of Richard's radical proposal,
sentences.zh: 虽然她不是理查德激进提议的粉丝，

sentences.en: Sandy Knapp proudly officiated those changes
sentences.zh: 但桑迪·纳普自豪地主持了这些变更，

sentences.en: at the 2024 International Botanical Congress in Madrid.
sentences.zh: 在2024年马德里国际植物学大会上。

sentences.en: And one of the proposals that was voted in
sentences.zh: 其中一项被投票通过的提案是

sentences.en: is to take all of the species names which are based on the epithet kafra.
sentences.zh: 将所有基于“kafra”这一加词的物种名称全部修改。

sentences.en: Kafra is derived from a word that is a racial slur in South Africa.
sentences.zh: “Kafra”源自一个在南非带有种族歧视色彩的词汇。

sentences.en: And that, for me, is actually important to recognize
sentences.zh: 对我而言，认识到这一点非常重要，

sentences.en: that that's something that needs to be changed.
sentences.zh: 因为这确实是需要改变的事情。

sentences.en: It's very, very offensive.
sentences.zh: 这非常、非常具有冒犯性。

sentences.en: It's offensive to a group of people.
sentences.zh: 它冒犯了一群人。

sentences.en: All of those names were changed,
sentences.zh: 所有这些名称都被修改了，

sentences.en: would take the C away, and they become AFRA.
sentences.zh: 去掉了其中的字母C，变成了“AFRA”。

sentences.en: To do this, the Congress exploited a loophole
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，大会利用了一个漏洞，

sentences.en: that allows scientific names to be corrected if they are misspelled.
sentences.zh: 即允许对拼写错误的学名进行修正。

sentences.en: It gave delegates an opportunity to vote for this one specific change
sentences.zh: 这让代表们有机会投票支持这一特定修改，

sentences.en: without committing to some groundbreaking new position on naming more broadly.
sentences.zh: 而无需在更广泛的命名问题上做出任何开创性的新立场。

sentences.en: Everyone was very respectful.
sentences.zh: 每个人都非常尊重彼此。

sentences.en: You know, well, if they weren't respectful, I would have kicked them out.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果他们不尊重，我早就把他们赶出去了。

sentences.en: But they were very respectful.
sentences.zh: 但他们表现得非常尊重。

sentences.en: And then we ran it, I ran it as a secret ballot.
sentences.zh: 然后我们进行了投票，我以无记名投票的方式进行。

sentences.en: So there was a, so you just wrote yes or no on your bit of paper
sentences.zh: 所以，你只需要在纸条上写下“是”或“否”，

sentences.en: and put it in a box and then it was counted.
sentences.zh: 放进盒子里，然后进行统计。

sentences.en: And it was 63%.
sentences.zh: 结果是63%的支持率。

sentences.en: It was an historic moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个历史性的时刻。

sentences.en: For the first time since Linnaeus came up with his binomial system,
sentences.zh: 自林奈提出双名法以来，这是第一次，

sentences.en: the offensive names of more than 200 plants, fungi and algae were changed.
sentences.zh: 超过200种植物、真菌和藻类的冒犯性名称被修改了。

sentences.en: As for Anophthalmos hitlery, I was surprised to learn that André is actually not all that concerned about the name.
sentences.zh: 至于希特勒盲步甲（Anophthalmos hitlery），我很惊讶地发现，安德烈其实并不太在意这个名字。

sentences.en: It's just a name for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它只是个名字。

sentences.en: For me it's important what kind of animal it is, where it lives, what it does,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，重要的是它是什么动物，它住在哪里，它做什么，

sentences.en: what it is, its position in ecology and everything.
sentences.zh: 它是什么，它在生态系统中的位置等等。

sentences.en: André was more interested in the beetle itself.
sentences.zh: 安德烈对甲虫本身更感兴趣。

sentences.en: I wasn't able to see one alive, but he had some dead Anophthalmos hitlery specimens
sentences.zh: 我没能见到活的，但他有一些死去的希特勒盲步甲标本，

sentences.en: he wanted to show me at his lab in Ljubljana, the Slovenian capital.
sentences.zh: 他想在位于斯洛文尼亚首都卢布尔雅那的实验室里给我看。

sentences.en: Inside, he pointed to five tiny insects pinned neatly in a row, the colour of aged bronze.
sentences.zh: 在里面，他指着五只整齐排列、呈古铜色的小昆虫。

sentences.en: So if you can see, it's a small, unremarkable, nothing to see actually, just a small beetle.
sentences.zh: 你看，它很小，平平无奇，其实没什么好看的，就是一只小甲虫。

sentences.en: Some people say, oh, it's just an ant, but it's not, it's a beetle.
sentences.zh: 有些人说，哦，那只是只蚂蚁，但它不是，它是甲虫。

sentences.en: Under a microscope, it was possible to see their slender, almost elegant features.
sentences.zh: 在显微镜下，可以看到它们纤细、近乎优雅的特征。

sentences.en: André says that the beetle evolved after an ancient ice age when living above ground became impossible.
sentences.zh: 安德烈说，这种甲虫是在远古冰河时代之后进化的，当时在地面上生活已变得不可能。

sentences.en: They couldn't live anymore in the soil, in the gravel or whatever.
sentences.zh: 它们无法再生活在土壤、砾石或任何地方了。

sentences.en: So they moved underneath.
sentences.zh: 所以它们搬到了地下。

sentences.en: And looking at this creature close up, you can appreciate how it evolved to suit a life in perpetual darkness.
sentences.zh: 近距离观察这种生物，你会惊叹于它是如何进化以适应永恒黑暗中的生活的。

sentences.en: If you live in a cave, you don't need ice.
sentences.zh: 如果你住在洞穴里，你就不需要眼睛。

sentences.en: It's just a waste of energy to produce ice.
sentences.zh: 产生眼睛只是浪费能量。

sentences.en: And they don't have pigment.
sentences.zh: 而且它们没有色素。

sentences.en: But they're all, oh, this, the colour of them is brownish-yellow.
sentences.zh: 但它们都是，哦，这个，它们的颜色是棕黄色的。

sentences.en: Hitler's beetle escaped from the worst conditions nature could throw at it.
sentences.zh: 希特勒盲步甲从大自然所能施加的最恶劣环境中幸存了下来。

sentences.en: It adapted and thrived in a new underground environment, where it lived out the next two million years.
sentences.zh: 它适应并繁衍于一个新的地下环境，并在那里度过了接下来的两百万年。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: So two million years of life, and then in the last, you know, less than a hundred years,
sentences.zh: 两百万年的生命，然后在过去，你知道，不到一百年的时间里，

sentences.en: it's named after the worst human in history.
sentences.zh: 它却以历史上最糟糕的人的名字命名。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, it's not its fault.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这不是它的错。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was reported this week by Will Aspinall, produced and edited by Emmett Fitzgerald,
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由Will Aspinall报道，Emmett Fitzgerald制作和编辑，

sentences.en: mixed by Martin Gonzalez, music by Swan Real, fact-checking by Graham Heysha.
sentences.zh: Martin Gonzalez混音，Swan Real配乐，Graham Heysha核实事实。

sentences.en: Kathy Tu is our executive producer, Kirk Colstead is the digital director, Delaney Hall is our senior editor.
sentences.zh: Kathy Tu是我们的执行制片人，Kirk Colstead是数字总监，Delaney Hall是我们的资深编辑。

sentences.en: The rest of the team includes Chris Berube, Jason DeLeon, Christopher Johnson, Vivian Leigh,
sentences.zh: 团队其他成员包括Chris Berube、Jason DeLeon、Christopher Johnson、Vivian Leigh、

sentences.en: Lash Madan, Joe Rosenberg, Kelly Prime, Jacob Medina-Gleason, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: Lash Madan、Joe Rosenberg、Kelly Prime、Jacob Medina-Gleason，以及我，Roman Mars。

sentences.en: The 99% Invisible logo was created by Stefan Lawrence.
sentences.zh: 《99% Invisible》的标志由Stefan Lawrence创作。

sentences.en: We are part of the SiriusXM podcast family, now headquartered six blocks north in the Pandora building,
sentences.zh: 我们是SiriusXM播客家族的一员，现在总部位于北边六个街区外的Pandora大楼，

sentences.en: in beautiful, uptown, Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 在美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心区。

sentences.en: You can find us all on Blue Sky, which is kind of like Twitter,
sentences.zh: 你们可以在Blue Sky上找到我们，它有点像Twitter，

sentences.en: but for people who don't think things should be named after Nazis,
sentences.zh: 但它是为那些认为不应该以纳粹名字命名事物的人准备的，

sentences.en: we're also hanging out on our own Discord server.
sentences.zh: 我们也在自己的Discord服务器上活跃。

sentences.en: There's a link to that, as well as every past episode of 99PI at 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 那里有链接，以及《99PI》往期的每一集，网址是99PI.org。
